{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABa1p2sQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhEbYuI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 105, "title": "Implement i486 CLTS (0F 06), reconcile CR0.TS/#NM, and audit related Ap protected-mode system instructions", "body": "## Problem

A user booting a locally held PC-98 HDD image named `aliceY3.hdi` on the **PC-9821Ap DOS** profile reports a new stop after the successful [#101/PR #102](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/102) paging-disabled protected-mode milestone and [#103/PR #104](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/104) STR/LTR/TSS initialization:

```text
unimplemented i486 opcode 0F 06
```

`0F 06` is Intel 386/486 **CLTS** (clear the Task-Switched bit of CR0), a system instruction frequently used in protected-mode FPU/task-state management. The current `Cpu::extended` handler in [`src/cpu.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/cpu.rs) does not implement it, despite `cr0: u32`, `MOV CRn`, `SMSW`, `LMSW` and some `EM/TS`-dependent x87 `#NM` checks already existing. The [protected-mode capability inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/protected-mode.md#focused-compatibility-inventory-and-cohesive-future-milestones) independently identifies CLTS as missing.

This is **one confirmed missing opcode**, not evidence that a real hardware task switch, paging, a complete x87, Windows, or an entire DOS extender is required. The user's private image was not available to the prior implementation agents; do not claim complete program boot after this fix.

## Expected outcome

Implement architecturally accurate **i386/i486 `CLTS`** in the original Rust CPU on the Ap profile, with correct state, privilege, instruction-length, prefix/invalid-encoding and exception behavior in both real and protected modes as specified by independent Intel 386/486 documentation. Verify that `CLTS` clears **only CR0.TS (bit 3)** and leaves all other CR0 bits, registers, flags, caches, RAM and device state intact. Keep `MOV CR0` readback, `SMSW`, `LMSW`, reset, and existing x87 `EM/TS` to `#NM` behavior coherent; do not silently run unimplemented numeric FPU operations.

**One-pass cluster rather than repeating one-opcode Issues:** in the same task, audit the **closely related protected-mode system instruction and CPU-state paths** in the existing code against the target architecture, and explicitly document coverage and next blocked feature *families*. Fix directly evidenced small, tightly coupled defects of `CR0.TS`/`#NM` lifecycle within this PR; for larger independent functionality (e.g., LAR/LSL/VERR/VERW/ARPL, debug registers, I/O privileges, real hardware task switching, paging and numerical x87), produce a prioritized grouped roadmap and separately scoped `task` Issues **only if reproducible evidence justifies them**. Do not make this task an open-ended claim of full i486 support or slip in unrelated emulator cores.

## Context and reproduction

User-reported progress with private `aliceY3.hdi` mounted as **IDE · HDI boot** on **PC-9821Ap DOS**:

1. `0F 20` CR read failure -> #97 / PR #98 implemented.
2. `0F 22` CR write failure -> #99 / PR #100 implemented.
3. `unsupported protected execution/paging transition`, **`PE=1 PG=0`** -> #101 / PR #102 implemented bounded paging-disabled protected mode.
4. `unsupported protected TSS/task register` -> #103 / PR #104 implemented STR/LTR and cached TSS initialization.
5. **New:** `unimplemented i486 opcode 0F 06` -> CLTS missing.

The reported error confirms an unsupported opcode was fetched; it does **not** reveal the actual CR0.TS value or whether an x87 operation/task switch follows. The current emulator supports a bounded ring-0 protected mode and x87 FNINIT/status metadata, not numerical x87 or general task switching.

Links:
- [src/cpu.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/cpu.rs)
- [docs/protected-mode.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/protected-mode.md)
- [docs/hardware.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware.md)
- [docs/dos-compatibility.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/dos-compatibility.md)
- [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) / [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md).

## Detailed implementation scope

1. **CLTS opcode/privilege:** decode `0F 06` with no ModR/M or immediate; use authoritative Intel 80386/80486 rules for its CPL0 restriction in protected mode (and permitted real-mode behavior), exceptions, legal prefixes and instruction boundary. On a rejected execution deliver the architecturally correct guest fault and restart state; do not incorrectly consume a following byte. Preserve the VM/V30 `0F` opcode interpretation.
2. **CR0 state:** clear exactly bit 3; keep PE, PG (if presently disabled), ET, EM, MP, NE, CD, NW and other implemented bits unchanged. Check observable readback via `0F 20`, SMSW and the x87 checks. Never clear CR0.EM as a workaround or allow an illegal mode transition.
3. **#NM and FPU coordination:** demonstrate that setting TS through legal CR0 operations causes the selected implemented x87 environment instruction(s) to fault consistently; CLTS then removes the TS-caused #NM condition, while EM still produces #NM independently. Retest behavior for both `FNINIT` and non-waiting status/control forms that the code *actually* supports. Undefined/unimplemented numerical FPU operations continue to diagnose honestly, not return fabricated mathematical results. Validate correct exception frames/IRET and no partial state mutation.
4. **One-pass coverage inventory:** enumerate and source-check related control/system instructions in Ap real/protected mode (CLTS, SMSW/LMSW, MOV CRn, SLDT/LLDT/STR/LTR, descriptor queries and other named unsupported system instructions) with current handler, instruction validity, available coverage, untested edge cases and realistic architectural *clusters* for next steps. Identify any tightly related `CR0.TS`/exception bugs with original regression probes and fix within scope. Document excluded broader work explicitly so developers need not wait for another private game error to discover known gaps. Do **not** open dozens of speculative instruction Issues.
5. **Diagnostics:** keep bounded CPU-only trace (mode, CS:EIP, `0F 06`, CR0 old/new incl. TS, execution result, fault metadata); never dump private guest code or full memory. The optional local user-HDI retest, if available legally, may identify the *next* actual compatibility blocker without making any assertion of playability.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce `unimplemented i486 opcode 0F 06` using an **independently authored, permissively licensed** guest running actual i486 CPU instructions in Ap mode; document reproducible source, checksum-pinned media and pre-fix trace without private media.
- [ ] Implement correct CLTS behavior (one opcode, correct consumed length, valid prefixes, CPL checks, error/fault restart handling) for Ap real and paging-disabled protected-mode contexts, with byte-precise source examples; preserve the independent VM/V30 decoder.
- [ ] Native tests exercise TS=0/1, EM=0/1, representative preserved CR0 bits, readback and SMSW, legal/illegal privilege and prefix cases, reset, EIP, flags, GPRs, segment/GDT/IDT/TR caches, and complete non-mutation on faults.
- [ ] Self-checking guest demonstrates TS set -> selected x87 #NM and valid fault-frame handling -> CLTS -> TS cleared and supported nonnumeric x87 execution -> EM #NM still enforced; do not claim numerical x87 fidelity. Where guest setup differs in real/protected mode, use separate fixture paths with clear deterministic markers and guards.
- [ ] Execute original tests with the **real Rust interpreter** natively and in **production Rust/Wasm** in Chromium for `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, cold boot and reset, verifying expected output/register/memory guards and no media mutation. No JS/host substitution for CPU semantics.
- [ ] Perform the **one-pass, documented architecture/coverage audit** of adjacent system-instruction/CR0.TS/#NM paths, recording accurate implemented/unsupported boundaries, linked tests and *grouped* follow-up milestones to reduce repeated one-opcode tasks. Small confirmed, directly related bugs should be fixed and regression-tested in this PR; defer independent substantial CPU subsystems to separately evidenced tasks.
- [ ] Preserve all existing VM/Ap protected mode, TSS/STR/LTR, PIC/PIT/FDC/IDE, DOS/ADV98/98VIDEOP, sound/graphics, wasm and static publication regressions. Run and record all existing fixture preparations, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, production Wasm build, publication audit, and real-Wasm Chromium suite **before merge**.
- [ ] Record optional `aliceY3.hdi` validation only if it is legally available privately; otherwise explicitly state unavailable and untested. Do not promise game boot/playability. Avoid any third-party emulator/chip library, translated/forked CPU core, proprietary NEC ROM/font, unlicensed disk or copyrighted game artifact in Git/CI/Pages.

All **mandatory** acceptance is machine-verifiable with original or clearly redistributable guest data. Human playtests, proprietary media, a live Pages site, physical PC-98 validation and checks possible only after merge must **not** be pre-merge blockers.

## Optional validation

Privately test the user-held `aliceY3.hdi` if legitimately accessible and record only short noncopyrighted CPU-state metadata on the next failure. A debug/trap or actual hardware-task-switch requirement, if discovered, should use cohesive independent Issues grounded in original CPU guest tests, not filename-specific hacks.

## Required post-merge verification

None. A deployment-only failure can be reported in a later separate `task` Issue and must not block merge.
